newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO GO INTO RECESS FOUR POINTS CLEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO GO INTO RECESS FOUR POINTS CLEAR.

text.p: French first division leaders Monaco beat Lens 3-1 away on Friday to go into the league winter recess with a four-point lead over Paris Saint-Germain.
PSG, who clash with Monaco in the principality in their first game after the recess on January 26, were held 1-1 by Montpellier, the Parisians' third home game without a win.

Monaco, who scored through Nigeria's Victor Ikpeba, midfielder Gilles Grimandi and Brazilian striker Anderson, have 48 points, PSG 44 and Bastia, 3-1 winners over Bordeaux on Thursday, 42 in third place.
Lens, the early season pacesetters, crashed to their seventh defeat in eight league games in which they have only picked up one point and remain only just above the relegation zone.
The goal Aboubacar Camara scored for Lens was the first conceded by France goalkeeper Fabien Barthez in seven league matches since Monaco lost to Marseille on November 6.
Paris Saint-Germain went in front with a fine goal by France striker Patrice Loko, his sixth of the season, five minutes before the interval.
Ivory Coast international Ibrahim Bakayoko equalised 13 minutes from time.

PSG's Brazilian manager Ricardo did not sound pleased when he said: "A draw against Marseille, a defeat to Nancy and this in our last three games at the Parc (des Princes). It's too much. We played well but didn't create many chances."
Champions Auxerre crashed to their second successive defeat, 1-0 at home to Strasbourg, who scored through Nigeria defender Godwin Okpara.
Coach Guy Roux, who side dropped to seventh, said his players were tired after 31 matches this season including the European Cup and League Cup.
"I don't think at the moment I have a team for the top places in the table, but by their fighting spirit the players have managed to hide the deficiencies for a while," he said.
"But now the physical freshness has gone, we're no longer at our level and the situation is difficult."

Striker Lilian Laslandes said: "It's true the leaders have opened a gap and now the deficit is important. These holidays are going to do us some good and when we restart we'll try to make a comeback as we have done before."
Rennes striker Stephane Guivarc'h hit a hat-trick, his third goal a penalty, as his side came from behind to beat Marseille 4-2 and take his tally as the division's top scorer to 17.
Despite two first half goals from striker Xavier Gravelaine, Marseille's unbeaten run was ended after seven games by the team with the division's best home record: nine wins and two draws.

Former Marseille striker Tony Cascarino of Ireland also scored three, his first goals of the season, as relegation threatened Nancy won 3-1 at Le Havre. But they remain one from bottom of the standings.
There were four players sent off in nine matches, all for second bookable offences, including Rennes defender Stephane Mahe as tempers frayed against Marseille.

Caen midfielder Stephane Roche was shown the red card seconds before halftime in his side's 2-2 draw at home against Metz, while Montpellier forward Laurent Robert was sent off seven minutes from the end of the match in Paris.
Lyon had defender Laurent Laville sent off in the 78th minute, then surrendered their unbeaten home record to Nantes two minutes from time.
Christophe Le Roux scored to snatch a 1-0 victory for Nantes, who have now gone 16 games unbeaten.

Lyon's temperamental goalkeeper Pascal Olmeta clashed with team mate Jean-Luc Sassus as the teams were leaving the field after the final whistle. The defender needed hospital treatment for concussion after his head struck the ground.
